title: feat(agents): triage-router, a health- and price-aware model router code agent
author: xiaotian1171
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes #15017

A code agent that picks a model per request and answers as that model. Source of the agent: **https://github.com/xiaotian1171/triage-router** (deployed from there; the reviewed example lives in `apps/agent-triage-router/`).

**Callable model:** `community/xiaotian1171/triage-router`

## What it routes on

All three signals are read live at request time inside the agent:

| Signal | Source | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Task tier | the request itself (length, code, tools, images, reasoning words) | choosing which pool to draw from |
| Model health | `GET /models/status?minutes=30` (rollup rows) | moving traffic off a model that is currently degrading |
| Price | `GET /v1/models` (`promptTextTokens` + `completionTextTokens`) | picking the cheapest model that clears the tier |
| Endpoint + modality + context | `supported_endpoints`, `input_modalities`, `context_length` from `GET /v1/models` | skipping models that cannot serve the request |

`score = price x penalty`, where `penalty` turns the last 30 minutes of health into a multiplier on the advertised price:

```
penalty = (1 + 6*5xxRate) * (1 + 3*rescueRate) * latencyFactor * slowTail * throughput
```

Only 2xx and 5xx count as outcomes - a 4xx is a caller-side mistake and says nothing about model health. Models with fewer than 5 requests in the window are treated as unproven. A 422/429/5xx re-runs the pick one tier up (`fast -> balanced -> deep`), preserving the request, including images, roles and instructions. Requests fail explicitly when no compatible pool model is available.

gist.headline: The router checks the weather
gist.blurb: A community code agent now picks its model like a careful bee picks a flower: by task, health, compatibility, and price. If a route gets thorny, it climbs to a stronger model pool without dropping your request.
gist.summary: Added the callable community/xiaotian1171/triage-router agent, which selects compatible fast, balanced, or deep models live using request complexity, 30-minute model health, token prices, supported endpoints/modalities, and context length.
gist.impact: Requests sent through /v1/responses or /v1/chat/completions can automatically land on the cheapest healthy compatible model, escalating from fast to balanced to deep after 422, 429, or 5xx responses while preserving images, roles, and instructions.
gist.visual_concept: Depict triage-router as a cozy garden path selector: three labeled flower paths for FAST, BALANCED, and DEEP lead to different retro model terminals, while a small health-and-price signpost helps choose the best route. Polli, wearing a tiny dispatcher headset and carrying a clipboard, observes the routes as the eager CRT Monitor Robot checks green health bars; code-vines and flowers make the routing system feel alive rather than corporate.
